answer_1.quote: We use GPT-4.1 to scale stance annotations for the remaining 130 videos.
answer_1.outputs: labels indicating whether videos support, oppose, or neither with respect to eight OUD-related myths

answer_2.quote: Tables 20-22 present the full evaluation of 10 LLMs, with details in §C.3. GPT-4o with few-shot prompting consistently outperformed other models, achieving 0.82-0.87 macro F1-scores across myths (Table ).

answer_3.quote: Following this approach, and in line with other works Park et al. ( ), we use the LLM-as-a-judge approach to assess and label the overall stance of the remaining 130 videos.

answer_4.quote: With the sampled videos, we conducted multiple rounds of annotations with six clinical researchers as experts using our annotation scheme ( §B.1), resulting in a gold-standard dataset of 2,480 high-quality labels (8 myths×310 videos).
answer_4.guideline: Experts assigned one of six labels: Opposes OUD Myths (-1), Neutral OUD Information (0), Supports OUD Myths (1), Irrelevant (2), URL Not Accessible (3), Non-English Language (4). For supporting or opposing videos, they specified the myth(s) involved, citing excerpts or timestamps. They reviewed metadata in priority order: title and description, then transcript. They provided a brief justification (∼10 words).
